To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the majority of CA1 pyramidal neurons in rats performing an episodic event memory task displayed event-specific discharge activities, which underwent transient theta phase-precession followed by sustained theta phase-locking.
hippocampal CA3 pyramidal neurons encode discrete event sequences in a rate and temporal code.

the majority of CA1 hippocampal neurons displayed sensory cue-specific, combination-specific, or choice-specific elevated discharge activities, and that the theta sequences of cell assemblies of the discrete event sequences had discrete event representations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of hippocampal neurons in the processing and storage of information about the environment.
the role of the hippocampus in the processing and memory of non-spatial information.
the question of how information is represented in neuronal systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hippocampus is a critical brain structure for memory and learning, but the exact mechanisms of how this is achieved is still unknown.
hippocampal theta sequences of event sequences have discrete representations.
hippocampal CA3-CA1 cell assemblies can represent discrete event sequences in a temporally precise manner, which may be the basis for episodic memory formation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hippocampus encodes episodic events as discrete representations, which are formed by the temporal and rate coding in single CA1 neurons.
CA1 neurons encode the episodic event sequences in the cue-combination tasks by a combination of rate coding and temporal coding.
the hippocampal CAI neurons encode discrete events in a temporally precise manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hippocampal cells can encode the temporal order of discrete events, and that the theta rhythm plays an important role in the temporal coding.
the hippocampus is not only a space encoder.
hippocampal neurons can be highly selective to discrete events, and their activities are temporally structured to form event-specific cell assemblies.
